page.layout: Running head top centre, with page number 271 at top right. Below it, one full-width block of text: a note in the same type as the body (Lecturi praecepta...), then the line Hactenus est Rhetorica explicita. Then a rule. Then the division title DE POETICA. and running text in one full-width column with German glosses in black letter. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: Lecturi praecepta prolixiora videant Rhetoricam
Domini Philippi Melanchthonis, & libros
quatuor Rhetoricorum ad Herennium.
Hactenus est Rhetorica explicita.
DE POETICA.
Quid est Poetica?
POETICA est ars bene versificandi,

l.bl: Die reymekunst ist eine kunst wol sprüche

main_text.l: Quot sunt consideranda in versibus?
Tria: Quantitas Syllabarum, Pedes, & Metrum.
Quid de quantitate Syllabarum dicis?
Omnis syllaba, aut est longa, aut brevis, aut communis.
Quænam Syllaba est longa?
Primò, omnis diphthongus est longa, ut prima syl-
laba in ætas, ein jetlichs alter / audio, ich höre / coena,
ein nachtmal / euge, ei wolan.
Secundò, omnis positio est longa. Est autem posi-
tio, quando vocalem sequuntur duæ cõsonæ, aut du-
plex: ut, Ast, aber / pax, friede / gaza, ein schatz / ajo, ich
sage. Cæterum cum prioris vocis ultima syllaba de-
finit in vocalem, & in proxima voce sequuntur duæ
vel plures consonæ, aut duplex, nulla fit inde necessa-
ria positio: ut, jam medio apparet fluctu nemorosa
Zacynthus, Virgil. Es erscheinet mitten in den was-

l.bl: sern die waldechtige Insel im Meer Jonio.

main_text.l: Si aut prioris vocis ultima definit in consonã, & in
proxima voce cõsona aut duplex sequitur, positio locum
habet: ut, nec te collaudes, nec te culpaveris ipse, Hoc
faciunt stulti, quos gloria vexat inanis, Du solt Dich sel[?]

page.notes: The big initial of POETICA is an ornamented capital that I could not identify with certainty; it reads as a P with decoration and is transcribed as P. The top-left mark before Lecturi and the small mark left of "pxima" are printer's ornaments or reference signs, not text; no matching note is printed. The last word is cut off at the foot of the page (sel with a trailing mark). Long s is normalised to s. German words set in black letter are marked with bl.
